title: Artinian infinitesimal criterion for etaleness at a point
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings essentially of finite type [def-weil-essentially-finite-type], let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ be an ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subseteq B$ lie over $\mathfrak m_A$. If for every $n\ge0$ the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I^{n+1}B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ is etale at the point $\mathfrak q/I^{n+1}B$ [def-weil-etale-at-a-point], then $A\to B$ is etale at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-etale-at-a-point].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43, Tag 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), proof of (2), invoking Lemma lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point; etale-at-a-point terminology is Morphisms, Definition 02GI and local criterion Lemma 02GU

mathlib_searches.query: Noetherian local ring map essentially finite type etale along an ideal if all I-adic infinitesimal quotients are etale
mathlib_searches.results: FormallyEtale, IsEtale, Scheme.Etale; no I-adic infinitesimal criterion

mathlib_searches.query: etale morphism detected on every Artinian quotient of local ring at a point
mathlib_searches.results: IsEtale.of_comp and Algebra.mem_etaleLocus_iff concern composition and etale locus, not detection via Artinian quotients
formal-etale and standard-etale lifting results occur; no theorem recovering etaleness from all Artinian neighbourhoods
